FEAR: Fear is older than Tartaria. It outlived the Giants. It will outlive you.
The Aether tastes your dread. Some say it feeds.
Hold still. The mud listens for trembling feet.
There is a sound the Aetherstone makes when a heart begins to break. I have heard it before.
Run if you must. The ruins have outrun braver souls.
Even the Sentinels paused, once. Then they remembered their orders.
Your breath has changed. So has the air.
Tartaria killed gods. You are not yet a god.
Do not look behind you. Whatever waits there has been waiting longer than your bloodline.
The Flood took those who closed their eyes. And those who kept them open.
Fear is a kind of seeing. Use it.
The dust on these stones remembers screaming.
CURIOSITY: Every question you ask, the Aether answers in its own time. Rarely in your language.
The Giants were curious, once. Their cities are buried beneath their answers.
Look closer. The walls of Tartaria were written, not built.
Knowledge here is a weight, not a wing.
Aetherstone hums different beneath a curious hand. Notice that.
Few who ask the right question survive the reply.
There is a door in everything. The trouble is recognising the hinge.
The Forgotten Order spent generations on questions you ask in passing. Do not waste their inheritance.
Tartaria left no manuals. Only invitations.
Every relic was meant for someone. It is rarely the one who finds it.
Curiosity carried the runecasters far. Some came back changed. Some came back nothing.
Trace the rune with your eyes, not your fingers. Not yet.
Children of the Unknowing Masses dismissed all of this as story. The story is still here.
AGGRESSION: The Giants struck first, too. Their bones are part of the road now.
Anger is honest. Tartaria respects honesty, briefly.
Steel cools faster in this mud. Strike clean.
There are things in these ruins that hunger to be hit. Be sure of which you are facing.
A drawn blade is a promise. The Aether keeps count of them.
Even the Sentinels know the difference between fury and intent.
Rage is fuel. Fuel runs out.
The Mud Monarchs taught the world to mistake violence for rule. Do not flatter them.
Kill if you must. Remember what was killed for.
The runecasters who fought best fought last.
Tartaria fell because someone could not stop pushing. Push wisely.
Wrath wakes the buried things. Quietly, then all at once.
CAUTIOUSNESS: Good. The buried cities reward a slow step.
Aetheric anomalies do not announce themselves. Neither should you.
A careful traveller leaves Tartaria. A reckless one becomes Tartaria.
The Sentinels measure intent before they measure threat. Give them little of either.
Listen. The stone is not always stone.
Patience kept the Forgotten Order alive while emperors fell.
Test the ground. Test the air. Test the silence.
Tartaria buries its secrets in layers. So do its traps.
There is wisdom in hesitation here. Foolishness elsewhere, perhaps. Not here.
A held breath has saved more expeditions than a drawn weapon.
Mud remembers every footprint. Walk as if it must forget yours.
The Aetherstone watches calm minds with less interest. Use that.
RESOLVE: Then walk. The ruins will weigh you regardless.
Tartaria did not fall to those who chose. It fell to those who hesitated.
Resolve is a flame the Aether cannot read. Keep it small. Keep it lit.
The Aetherborn felt it too, the moment before their blood remembered.
Many have stood where you stand. Few stood as long as you mean to.
Hold to your purpose. The mud takes what is not held.
A vow spoken in these ruins echoes longer than stone.
The Giants ruled by certainty. Their certainty buried them. Mind that.
Step forward. The relics rarely come to the still.
Your bones know what your mouth has not yet said. Let them.
The Forgotten Order calls this the marrow-hour. The moment one becomes worth remembering.
Tartaria is not impressed. It is, however, watching.
DESPAIR: Despair is the Flood's last gift. It still arrives on time.
Many who knelt in these ruins never stood again. A few did. Few is enough.
The Aetherstone glows brightest near the broken.
Even the Giants wept, in the end. The mud took those tears too.
Hope was buried with Tartaria. Not destroyed. Buried.
I have watched empires lose what you are losing. Empires came back. Slowly.
The world above forgot Tartaria entirely. Forgetting is also a kind of survival.
The Mud Seas drown louder voices than yours. They have not drowned you yet.
Sit, if you must. The ruins are patient with the still.
A heart this heavy sinks faster. Take less weight into the next step.
There are runes for grief. None of them mend it. All of them carry it.
Tartaria is a long argument with despair. So far, it is winning. So far.
